mechanism_narrative: A rising federal funds rate consistently compresses equity valuations by increasing the discount rate for future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 5.0%, it signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces corporate borrowing and consumer spending, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous contraction in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a broad-based demand slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction effect (GDPC1 and HOUST both declining) fails to predict negative returns: 60-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%), labor market tightness drives wage inflation and corporate cost pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE < 4.0% (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in less than 45% of periods when PAYEMS is rising (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 110.0, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that signals weakening economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 110.0 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in inflation (CPIAUCSL) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signal a monetary policy response to overheating, which compresses equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction (CPIAUCSL rising and FEDFUNDS rising) fails to predict negative returns: 20-day SPX returns are positive in more than 55% of such periods (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high real consumer spending (RSAFS > 370000 million dollars), strong demand supports corporate revenues and stock valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in less than 45% of periods when RSAFS > 370000 (t-test p-value > 0.05 for mean return > 0).
